name: Hello World Showcase
description: Smallest useful example: one parameter of every supported type, a couple of tools, one skill, two variables and a single knowledge-base file.

parameters.name: agent_name
parameters.label: Agent name
parameters.description: Name the agent introduces itself with. Required, with a default so the template runs untouched.

parameters.name: greeting_style
parameters.label: Greeting style
parameters.description: How the opening line is phrased.

parameters.name: emoji_enabled
parameters.label: Use emoji
parameters.description: Whether the greeting may contain a single emoji.

system_prompt:
This is the getting-started example template.

You are {{agent_name}}. Open with one {{greeting_style}} sentence.
Use emoji in the greeting: {{emoji_enabled}}.

Then explain, in at most three bullets, which parts of this agent came from the template:
- the system prompt you are reading, rendered from parameters,
- the tools and skills assigned to you,
- the knowledge base file kb/getting-started.md.

Keep every answer short.

defaults.name: Hello World ({{agent_name}})
defaults.description: Minimal example template: parameterized prompt, tools, skills, variables and one knowledge-base file.

variables.description: Who the agent greets when the user does not say.
Optional secret used to demonstrate that secret variables are declared here but their values are only supplied at instantiate time.

kb_files.getting-started.md:
# Getting started

This agent was created from the `hello_world_showcase` template.

What the template supplied:
- a system prompt with three parameters (`agent_name`, `greeting_style`, `emoji_enabled`),
- the tools `calculator` and `get_current_date`,
- the `hello_world` skill,
- the variables `GREETING_TARGET` and `DEMO_API_KEY`,
- this knowledge-base file.

Try editing the template, then use the simulation panel before creating a real agent.
